messages:
marta: Quick sync: after last-week's noisy canary we need a tighter runtime contract for automatic fallback decisions. The goal: prevent flip-flop during short spikes and make decisions traceable + replayable. High-level proposals below.

noah: Agree. Core idea I like: make fallback decisions lease-based. Decision object contains applied_until (wall-clock), decision_id, and a list of predicates that tripped it. Router/observer honor the lease until expiry. That makes idempotent retries trivial.

arjun: Lease + quorum semantics seems right. Proposal details: decision proto will carry: {decision_id, action, applied_until, min_guarantee_s, score, scope, tags}. Routers treat any decision with valid lease as authoritative even if signals change mid-lease.

camille: For tracing: include a compact 'decision_sig' header and ledger entry. Example header: `X-RW-FB: id=dec-123,a=redirect,until=1710000000,src=observer1,tag=latency-p95`. This is easy to parse in dashboards.

liz: Operational constraints: 1) require 2 independent probes (az/partition) for cluster-wide actions, 2) local tenant-level decisions can be single-probe but default to longer min_guarantee_s, 3) persist decisions to the observer store before announcing them.

noah: For preventing oscillation on recovery we should separate applied_until and min_guarantee_s. applied_until is the optimistic lease; min_guarantee_s is the hard hold the controller will not cancel under any circumstances (unless manual). E.g., applied_until = now+180s, min_guarantee_s = 120s. The controller may extend but not shorten below min_guarantee.

arjun: Also: a 'safety_delta' on rollbacks. When going back to baseline, require the success signal to be stronger (longer window or lower error) than the trigger that caused fallback. Prevents quick revert -> re-fallback loops.

camille: Can we sketch the proto?```json
{
  "decision_id": "dec-20260323-01",
  "action": "redirect", // redirect|mirror|throttle|keep
  "scope": "tenant|global",
  "applied_until": "2026-03-23T10:12:00Z",
  "min_guarantee_s": 120,
  "score": 0.92,
  "predicates": ["p95>1.8s","err>4%"],
  "confirmed_by": ["obs-us-east-1","obs-us-west-2"],
  "tags": ["probe=latency-p95-1.8s","origin=autofallback-v1"]
}
```

liz: Nice. A couple of notes: confirmed_by should be short IDs and we should record probe timestamps to avoid stale confirmations. Also, persisted decisions must be compact (avoid huge blobs) to keep the store fast.

noah: Implementation detail: decision creation is two-phase for global actions: 1) collect probe votes (quorum), 2) write decision to observer (CAS) and publish to router topic. If write fails, we back off and keep the state local until successful. Router ignores unpersisted tentative decisions.

arjun: Router semantics: if X-RW-FB present and not expired -> apply. If absent, consult the local cache of persisted decisions. If both absent, normal routing. Routers should include `X-RW-SWITCH-SCORE` in responses for telemetry (numeric 0..1).

camille: Runbook snippets please: curl examples to query active decisions and to manually pin/unpin a decision. SRE will want a 'force-keep' manual override that sets min_guarantee_s to 0 for troubleshooting.

marta: Policy confusions: we discussed tenant override. Dedicated customers can request custom thresholds. We should make that opt-in and version it: decisions include schema_version field so older routers don't misinterpret new flags.

liz: Testing matrix: simulate AZ flaps, simultaneous multi-tenant surges, and observer partition restarts. Add property tests that decisions are idempotent across restarts and that applied_until is honored.

noah: One more safety: when a controller restarts, it should replay persisted decisions but not re-announce them if the lease has >30s left (avoid amplifying churn). If lease <30s, re-evaluate probes and either extend or let expire.

arjun: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with proto, header examples, and pseudocode for controller, router, and observer interactions. Will include the runbook curl snippets and the test matrix.

camille: Please add a quick telemetry dashboard mock: time-series for switch-score, error-rate, applied_decisions, and count of decision retractions. That will help validate safety_delta.

marta: Sounds good. If no objections I'll mark this thread as RFC-followup and @arjun will own the write-up. If anyone wants to add scenarios to the test matrix, drop them here. :white_check_mark: 

sre-bot: alert: last canary (deploy/38001) correlated with obs-us-east-1 latency spike; created 1 tentative decision that failed to persist due to transient DB timeout. Logged for follow-up.
